title: Where the Profit Comes From
endLine: From glucose, net ATP equals the new phosphates an oxidation pays for.

scenes.tts: The first film did the arithmetic. Spend two A T P, earn four, keep two. But each half of the sugar carries one ordinary phosphate. So how does each half hand two phosphates to A D P?
scenes.narration: The first film did the arithmetic. Spend two ATP, earn four, keep two. But each half of the sugar carries one ordinary phosphate. So how does each half hand two phosphates to ADP?
scenes.caption: The first film did the arithmetic. Spend two ATP, earn four, keep two. But each half of the sugar carries one ordinary phosphate. So how does each half hand two phosphates to ADP?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map: BLUE = carbon (the sugar and its halves), YELLOW = ATP and any phosphate that came from ATP, RED = ATP spent, GREEN = ATP earned / gain, TEAL = NAD+, PURPLE = NADH, GREY = structure. New in this film: MAGENTA = a new phosphate captured from inorganic phosphate. GOLD (the first film's checkpoint colour) is not used. No molecular structures: a sugar half is a BLUE rounded bar with three small BLUE carbon dots; a phosphate is a small round token. OPENING (recap): the first film's YELLOW coin ledger appears across the top third: two RED-ringed YELLOW coins slide out labelled 'spent 2', four GREEN-ringed YELLOW coins slide in labelled 'earned 4', and a tally reads 'net +2'. On 'each half of the sugar', the camera drops to the lower two thirds: one large BLUE sugar half (filling about 60% of the frame height with its token) carrying ONE small YELLOW phosphate token at its right end, labelled 'one ordinary phosphate'. Beside it, two empty GREY ADP slots wait, each labelled 'ADP'. On the question, two ghost arrows reach from the single token to both slots; one arrow has nothing to carry and a large white '?' appears between them. Large white text at the top: 'One phosphate in, two out?' Ambient: the carbon dots jiggle gently in the bar.

Title 'Where the Profit Comes From' fades in for 2 s above the BLUE sugar half while the question text fades out. The YELLOW token pulses softly; the two ADP slots stay empty. The coin ledger shrinks to a small strip at the top edge, where it stays for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: Phosphates sit on a ladder, ranked by how eager they are to leave. A T P sits at minus thirty point five kilojoules per mole. On this standard ladder, a kinase can load A D P favorably only from a higher rung. The sugar half's phosphate is an ordinary one, far below.
scenes.narration: Phosphates sit on a ladder, ranked by how eager they are to leave. ATP sits at −30.5 kJ/mol. On this standard ladder, a kinase can load ADP favorably only from a higher rung. The sugar half's phosphate is an ordinary one, far below.
scenes.caption: Phosphates sit on a ladder, ranked by how eager they are to leave. ATP sits at −30.5 kJ/mol. On this standard ladder, a kinase can load ADP favorably only from a higher rung. The sugar half's phosphate is an ordinary one, far below.
scenes.visual: The ONE world of the film appears and stays: a tall vertical GREY ladder fills the LEFT 40% of the frame and about 75% of its height; the BLUE sugar half and the ADP slots sit at RIGHT. The ladder is drawn TO SCALE from the lesson's standard hydrolysis values, axis 'ΔG°′ of hydrolysis (kJ/mol)', higher rungs = more negative = more eager to leave, from −65 at top to −10 at bottom. On 'ranked', rungs light up one at a time with short labels: 'ATP −30.5' (YELLOW, at -30.5), 'ordinary ester −13.8' (GREY-WHITE, at -13.8). Two upper rungs appear as faint unlabelled outlines at -49.3 and -61.9, waiting. On 'only from a higher rung', a GREEN arrow slides down from just above the ATP rung into the ADP slot, and a RED arrow trying to go up from the low rung to ATP bounces back with a small cross. On 'far below', the YELLOW token on the sugar half is linked by a thin dotted line to the 'ordinary ester' rung and bobs there; a small tag reads 'like glucose-6-phosphate'. At most 6 labelled items on screen.

scenes.tts: So the cell builds a higher rung. At step six, an enzyme oxidizes the sugar half, and N A D plus takes the electrons. Done in one go, that energy would be lost as heat. Instead, the enzyme holds it in an activated bond.
scenes.narration: So the cell builds a higher rung. At step 6, an enzyme oxidizes the sugar half, and NAD+ takes the electrons. Done in one go, that energy would be lost as heat. Instead, the enzyme holds it in an activated bond.
scenes.caption: So the cell builds a higher rung. At step 6, an enzyme oxidizes the sugar half, and NAD+ takes the electrons. Done in one go, that energy would be lost as heat. Instead, the enzyme holds it in an activated bond.
scenes.visual: Same world. A GREY enzyme cartoon (a simple rounded clamp, labelled 'step 6 enzyme', no structure) closes on the LEFT end of the BLUE sugar half, the end without the phosphate. On 'oxidizes', a TEAL 'NAD+' token arrives, two small white electron dots hop from the sugar half onto it, and it turns PURPLE, relabelled 'NADH', and drifts off to the corner. On 'lost as heat', a ghost version shows the energy escaping as wavy orange-red heat lines that fade away (tag 'one go: heat'), then rewinds. On 'activated bond', the clamp's grip on the sugar half becomes a short bright glowing link, labelled 'activated bond'. The ladder at left stays; the faint rung at -49.3 begins to glow.

scenes.tts: Then inorganic phosphate, from the cell's pool, not from A T P, attacks that bond and carries the sugar half away. Its new phosphate sits at minus forty-nine point three, well above A T P. At step seven, a kinase hands it to A D P.
scenes.narration: Then inorganic phosphate, from the cell's pool, not from ATP, attacks that bond and carries the sugar half away. Its new phosphate sits at −49.3 kJ/mol, well above ATP. At step 7, a kinase hands it to ADP.
scenes.caption: Then inorganic phosphate, from the cell's pool, not from ATP, attacks that bond and carries the sugar half away. Its new phosphate sits at −49.3 kJ/mol, well above ATP. At step 7, a kinase hands it to ADP.
scenes.visual: A loose MAGENTA phosphate token labelled 'inorganic phosphate' drifts in from a small pool of MAGENTA dots at the bottom edge. It strikes the glowing link; the clamp opens and releases the BLUE sugar half, which now carries TWO tokens: the new MAGENTA one at its left end and the old YELLOW one at its right. Label under the bar: '1,3-BPG'. A dotted line links the MAGENTA token to the ladder, and the rung at -49.3 lights fully, labelled '1,3-BPG −49.3' in MAGENTA, clearly above the YELLOW ATP rung. On 'step 7', the MAGENTA token slides down the ladder past the ATP rung (GREEN arrow) and drops into the first ADP slot, which becomes a YELLOW coin with a MAGENTA rim, labelled 'ATP'. A GREEN '+1' pops beside it.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to hold. From glucose, the net gain is exactly the new phosphate that this oxidation captures. Everything else the cell hands to A D P is only paid back.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to hold. From glucose, the net gain is exactly the new phosphate that this oxidation captures. Everything else the cell hands to ADP is only paid back.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea to hold. From glucose, the net gain is exactly the new phosphate that this oxidation captures. Everything else the cell hands to ADP is only paid back.
scenes.visual: The new MAGENTA-rimmed ATP coin glows and slides up to the ledger strip at the top, settling under 'net +2' with a small MAGENTA tag 'new'. The PURPLE NADH token in the corner pulses once at the same moment, tying the gain to the oxidation. Large white text at centre for the length of the scene: 'Net gain = new phosphate'. On 'only paid back', the YELLOW token still on the sugar half pulses, tagged 'paid back'. The ladder stays at left.

scenes.tts: But that old phosphate is still on the sugar half, below A T P. There is no second oxidation. So how can it make A T P?
scenes.narration: But that old phosphate is still on the sugar half, below ATP. There is no second oxidation. So how can it make ATP?
scenes.caption: But that old phosphate is still on the sugar half, below ATP. There is no second oxidation. So how can it make ATP?
scenes.visual: The centre text fades. Camera eases toward the BLUE sugar half, now carrying only its YELLOW token (label under the bar changes to '3-phosphoglycerate'). The dotted line from the YELLOW token runs to the low 'ordinary ester' rung, far below ATP. The second ADP slot waits, empty. The top rung at -61.9 is still a faint, unlabelled outline. Question card at the top in white: 'Old phosphate, no oxidation: how?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. The YELLOW token bobs gently at the low rung; the empty ADP slot pulses faintly; the faint top rung shimmers. No other change.

scenes.tts: Rearrange the molecule. Step eight slides the phosphate from carbon three to carbon two. Step nine pulls off water, making P E P. That barely changes the free energy. Yet P E P's phosphate sits at the top of the ladder, minus sixty-one point nine.
scenes.narration: Rearrange the molecule. Step 8 slides the phosphate from carbon 3 to carbon 2. Step 9 pulls off water, making PEP. That barely changes the free energy. Yet PEP's phosphate sits at the top of the ladder, −61.9 kJ/mol.
scenes.caption: Rearrange the molecule. Step 8 slides the phosphate from carbon 3 to carbon 2. Step 9 pulls off water, making PEP. That barely changes the free energy. Yet PEP's phosphate sits at the top of the ladder, −61.9 kJ/mol.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. On 'step eight', the three carbon dots in the BLUE bar are numbered 1, 2, 3 and the YELLOW token slides from the dot marked 3 to the dot marked 2. On 'pulls off water', a small pale water droplet lifts out of the bar and floats away; the bar's outline snaps into a slightly tenser shape, labelled 'PEP'. On 'barely changes', a small GREY gauge beside the bar labelled 'free-energy change: small' barely twitches (schematic). On 'top of the ladder', the dotted line from the YELLOW token leaps from the low rung up to the top rung, which lights fully, labelled 'PEP −61.9'. The YELLOW token now glows brightly.

scenes.tts: The secret is what stays behind. Once the phosphate leaves, the rest is an unstable form that quickly settles into pyruvate. So this phosphate leaves very readily. At step ten, a kinase hands it to A D P.
scenes.narration: The secret is what stays behind. Once the phosphate leaves, the rest is an unstable form that quickly settles into pyruvate. So this phosphate leaves very readily. At step 10, a kinase hands it to ADP.
scenes.caption: The secret is what stays behind. Once the phosphate leaves, the rest is an unstable form that quickly settles into pyruvate. So this phosphate leaves very readily. At step 10, a kinase hands it to ADP.
scenes.visual: A ghost preview: the YELLOW token lifts off; the remaining BLUE bar wobbles (tag 'unstable form') and then settles into a calm, rounder BLUE bar labelled 'pyruvate'. The ghost rewinds once, then plays for real on 'step ten': the YELLOW token slides down the ladder from the top rung past the ATP rung (GREEN arrow) and drops into the second ADP slot, which becomes a plain YELLOW ATP coin. The sugar half settles as 'pyruvate'. Small tag on the second coin: 'paid back'.

scenes.tts: Now count phosphate groups for one glucose. Four leave to A D P. Two only repay the A T P spent at steps one and three. Two are new, taken from inorganic phosphate at step six. The oxidation paid for those two.
scenes.narration: Now count phosphate groups for one glucose. Four leave to ADP. Two only repay the ATP spent at steps 1 and 3. Two are new, taken from inorganic phosphate at step 6. The oxidation paid for those two.
scenes.caption: Now count phosphate groups for one glucose. Four leave to ADP. Two only repay the ATP spent at steps 1 and 3. Two are new, taken from inorganic phosphate at step 6. The oxidation paid for those two.
scenes.visual: The world widens: a second, identical BLUE sugar half slides in beside the first (label 'two halves, same steps'), and each plays its two hand-offs quickly, so four coins line up at the bottom right. The ledger strip at the top grows back to full size. Two coins (the plain YELLOW ones from step 10) slide up to sit under the two RED 'spent 2' coins and cancel them, tag 'repay steps 1, 3'. The two MAGENTA-rimmed coins (from step 7) slide up under 'net +2', tag 'new, from step 6'. Two PURPLE NADH tokens sit beside them. A small tag at the bottom edge reads 'counting groups, not atoms'. At most 6 labelled items on screen.

scenes.tts: So the two phosphates lent by A T P only break even. Every A T P glycolysis nets from glucose was paid for by the oxidation at step six, which needs N A D plus.
scenes.narration: So the two phosphates lent by ATP only break even. Every ATP glycolysis nets from glucose was paid for by the oxidation at step 6, which needs NAD+.
scenes.caption: So the two phosphates lent by ATP only break even. Every ATP glycolysis nets from glucose was paid for by the oxidation at step 6, which needs NAD+.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: the ladder at left with all four rungs lit, the two pyruvate halves at right, the ledger strip at top. On 'break even', the YELLOW coins and the RED spent coins pulse together and fade to a calm '0'. On 'paid for by the oxidation', the two MAGENTA-rimmed coins glow and a MAGENTA line traces back from them to the 1,3-BPG rung and to the step 6 enzyme clamp. On 'needs NAD plus', the two PURPLE NADH tokens pulse. MAGENTA inorganic phosphate dots keep drifting slowly in the pool at the bottom edge.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (MAGENTA phosphate dots drifting in the pool, the ladder faintly lit, the two MAGENTA-rimmed coins glowing). Large centred white text: 'From glucose, net ATP equals the new phosphates an oxidation pays for.'
